title: Exact gravitational waves
one_line_summary: Leaves linearized theory behind and builds exact vacuum wave spacetimes by imposing two commuting spacelike symmetries: cylindrical Einstein-Rosen waves (a flat-space wave equation plus quadratures), plane waves in Rosen and Brinkmann coordinates, delta-function impulsive waves, and the Penrose-Khan and Szekeres collisions in which two plane waves focus each other into a spacelike singularity.
role_in_book: Chapter 21 treated gravitational radiation as a small ripple on flat space-time, where waves superpose and never interact. This short chapter is the book's first look at what the full non-linear field equations say about radiation. It reuses the Killing-vector machinery of Chapter 7, Birkhoff's theorem from Chapter 15, the conformal flatness of 2-metrics from Section 6.13 and the h22 wave of Section 21.4, and it sets up the double-null, characteristic-data viewpoint that Chapter 23 (Bondi radiation, characteristic initial value problem, Petrov types) develops systematically. It also echoes the black-hole chapters by showing that singularities are not merely artefacts of spherical symmetry: colliding waves generate them too.

learning_objectives: Reader can explain why spherical symmetry cannot support vacuum gravitational waves (Birkhoff) and why two commuting spacelike Killing vectors are the natural next symmetry assumption.
Reader can tell cylindrical from plane symmetry by the topology (circle versus line) of the Killing orbits.

Reader can reduce a whole-cylinder-symmetric metric to the Einstein-Rosen form (22.4) using a new radial coordinate built from the Killing-orbit areas and the conformal flatness of the (t, rho) 2-metric.
Reader can state the Einstein-Rosen vacuum equations, recognise (22.5) as the flat cylindrical wave equation, and check the integrability condition that lets gamma be found by quadrature.
Reader can build Bessel-mode and Weber-Wheeler pulse solutions for psi and explain why the second-kind Bessel function is discarded.
Reader can start from the linearized h22 wave, promote it to the Rosen ansatz (22.10), compute its connection and curvature, and derive the single vacuum condition f''/f + g''/g = 0.
Reader can transform a Rosen plane wave into Brinkmann form (22.17) and use that form to explain why co-propagating plane waves superpose exactly while counter-propagating ones do not.

Reader can manipulate step and delta distributions (theta' = delta, u delta = 0) and verify that f = 1 + u theta, g = 1 - u theta is an impulsive plane wave with delta-function Riemann curvature and vanishing Ricci tensor.
Reader can distinguish impulsive waves from sandwich waves on a space-time diagram and describe what a geodesic observer feels crossing each.

Reader can read the Penrose-Khan diagram: identify the four regions, the flat versus curved parts, the fold (caustic) singularities at u = 1 and v = 1, and the spacelike curvature singularity u^2 + v^2 = 1.

Reader can explain why the singularity formed in colliding plane waves is unavoidable (spacelike) and why Szekeres' more general sandwich-wave collisions showed it is not an artefact of the impulsive idealization.
Reader can describe the colliding-wave problem as a characteristic initial value problem with data on two intersecting null hypersurfaces.

teaching_approach.summary: A compact, derivation-led survey. The authors let symmetry do the work: each section adds a symmetry assumption, adapts coordinates to it, and watches the vacuum field equations collapse to something solvable (a flat wave equation, a single ODE, a distributional identity). Linearized theory from Chapter 21 is used as the seed for the exact ansatz rather than as a separate topic. Several steps are delegated to exercises, and the final two sections switch to an outline of research results (Penrose-Khan, Szekeres), carried mainly by two space-time diagrams.
narrative_arc: Motivating question: can the full non-linear equations describe radiation exactly? Spherical symmetry is ruled out at once by Birkhoff's theorem.
Symmetry ladder: drop to two commuting spacelike Killing vectors; the orbit topology (S^1 x R versus R x R) splits the problem into cylindrical and plane waves.
Cylindrical model: adapt coordinates, impose reflection (whole-cylinder) symmetry, use conformal flatness of the 2-metric to reach the Einstein-Rosen metric.
Formalism payoff: the vacuum equations become a flat cylindrical wave equation for psi plus two first-order equations for gamma, consistent because of the wave equation.
Solutions and history: Bessel modes, then the Weber-Wheeler pulse that settled Einstein and Rosen's doubts about regularity and energy.
Plane model: take the linearized h22 metric in double null coordinates, square its coefficients to make an exact ansatz, compute curvature, find one ODE and an arbitrary profile h(u).
Change of viewpoint: Rosen to Brinkmann coordinates exposes h explicitly and reveals exact superposition for waves moving the same way, motivating the collision problem.
Idealize further: introduce distributions and build the impulsive plane wave, a null plane of delta curvature separating two flat regions; contrast with sandwich waves.
Application: glue two impulsive waves together (Penrose-Khan), map the four regions and the singularities on a space-time diagram.
Generalize and caution: Szekeres' characteristic-initial-value framework and sandwich collisions still produce singularities; later matter-coupled solutions raise interpretive controversies.
signature_moves: Using the orbit topology of the Killing vectors, rather than their algebra, to decide between cylindrical and plane waves.
Constructing the Einstein-Rosen radial coordinate as the square root of the product of the two Killing-orbit metric coefficients, so rho measures the area of the invariant 2-surfaces.
Promoting a linearized metric to an exact ansatz by writing its coefficients as squares, then testing it against the full field equations.
Presenting the same plane wave in two coordinate systems and reading different physics off each: Rosen for the metric functions and caustics, Brinkmann for the profile and superposition.
Treating the impulsive wave as the zero-thickness limit of a sandwich wave and doing the curvature calculation with elementary distribution identities.
Carrying the colliding-wave story almost entirely by a labelled (t, x) diagram with regions I-IV, marking where curvature is zero, delta-like, finite, or divergent.
Closing with explicit warnings that problem formulation and physical interpretation are delicate, rather than a tidy conclusion.

sections.title: Gravitational waves and symmetries
sections.summary: Explains the strategy of hunting for exact radiative vacuum solutions by assuming symmetry. Spherical symmetry fails because Birkhoff's theorem forces staticity. The next option is a pair of independent spacelike Killing vectors whose orbits form 2-surfaces; these are taken to commute. If one Killing vector has closed (circle) orbits and the other open (line) orbits the waves are cylindrical; if both are lines the waves are plane.
key_moves: Rule out spherical symmetry via Birkhoff's theorem.
Assume two independent spacelike Killing vectors with surface-forming orbits and deduce [V, W] = 0, citing (10.15).
Classify by topology of integral curves: S^1 and R gives cylindrical waves; R and R gives plane waves.

sections.title: Einstein-Rosen waves
sections.summary: Adapts coordinates (t, rho, phi, z) to rotational and translational Killing vectors, imposes reflection symmetry in phi and z to remove cross terms, defines a new radial coordinate from the orbit metric coefficients and a potential psi from the z-coefficient, and uses conformal flatness of the (t, rho) 2-metric to reach the Einstein-Rosen metric with two functions psi and gamma. The vacuum equations reduce to a flat-space cylindrical wave equation for psi and first-order equations for gamma whose compatibility follows from the wave equation. Separation of variables gives Bessel modes (regular J0 kept, singular N0 dropped), and the Weber-Wheeler superposition gives a regular, energy-carrying pulse, overturning Einstein and Rosen's initial scepticism.
key_moves: Discrete symmetries z -> -z and phi -> -phi eliminate all dphi dx^a and dz dx^a cross terms.
New radial coordinate rho = (CD)^{1/2} and psi = (1/2) ln D put the Killing part of the metric in the form rho^2 e^{-2psi} dphi^2 + e^{2psi} dz^2.
Any 2-metric is conformally flat, so the (t, rho) block becomes e^{2gamma - 2psi}(dt^2 - drho^2).
Vacuum equations split into a linear wave equation for psi (22.5) and quadratures for gamma (22.6)-(22.7).
Integrability gamma_{,rho t} = gamma_{,t rho} holds automatically because of (22.5).
Separable Bessel modes; discard N0 because it diverges on the axis.
Superpose modes with exponential weight into a pulse (22.9) whose closed form is a complex-conjugate pair, then integrate for gamma.

sections.title: Exact plane wave solutions
sections.summary: Introduces double null coordinates u = t - x, v = t + x and rewrites the linearized h22 wave as the Rosen line element du dv - f^2(u) dy^2 - g^2(u) dz^2. Treated as an exact ansatz, it has four non-zero Christoffel symbols, two independent Riemann components, and a single vacuum equation f''/f + g''/g = 0, so an arbitrary function h(u) generates a linearly polarized exact plane wave. A coordinate change gives the Brinkmann form with h appearing explicitly as the wave amplitude. The section then argues that GR has no general superposition principle, but plane waves travelling in the same direction superpose by adding their h functions; genuine scattering needs counter-propagating waves, and a boost can always make a collision head-on.
concepts: Rosen form of a plane wave
linearly polarized exact plane gravitational wave
Brinkmann form of a plane wave
exact superposition of co-propagating plane waves
key_moves: Square the metric functions of the linearized h22 wave so the signature is guaranteed, then drop the smallness assumption.
Compute Gamma^1_22 = 2ff', Gamma^1_33 = 2gg', Gamma^2_02 = f'/f, Gamma^3_03 = g'/g, and R_0202 = ff'', R_0303 = gg''.
The only vacuum equation is f''/f + g''/g = 0; name f''/f = h and solve g''/g = -h, so any h(u) works.
Transform (22.16) to Brinkmann coordinates where the metric is flat plus h(U)(Z^2 - Y^2) dU^2.
Linearity in h of the Brinkmann metric shows co-moving waves add; non-linearity must show up only in collisions.
Reduce oblique collisions to head-on ones by choosing a boosted observer (Exercise 4.10).

sections.title: Impulsive plane gravitational waves
sections.summary: Digresses to define the Heaviside step and Dirac delta (as a distribution) and records theta' = delta, u delta = 0, u theta' = 0. Choosing f = 1 + u theta(u), g = 1 - u theta(u) in the Rosen form satisfies the vacuum equation with f''/f = delta, so Ricci vanishes while Riemann (equal to Weyl in vacuum) has delta components on u = 0. In Brinkmann form h = delta, and off u = 0 the metric is Minkowski in null coordinates. The result is a single null plane of curvature (shock or impulsive wave) between two flat regions. A sandwich wave is defined as a curved vacuum slab bounded by flat regions; an observer crossing it feels a finite-duration transverse tidal effect, and the impulsive wave is its thin limit.
concepts: Weyl tensor equals Riemann tensor in vacuum
transverse tidal acceleration in a plane wave
key_moves: Establish theta' = delta by integrating against a test function and integrating by parts.
Use u delta(u) = 0 to show f' = theta exactly (the u delta term drops).
Evaluate f''/f = delta because f = 1 wherever delta is supported.
Read off R_0202 = -R_0303 = delta(u) and zero Ricci: curvature confined to the wavefront.
Brinkmann form with h = delta reduces to flat space for U != 0.
Interpret the impulsive wave as the zero-thickness limit of a sandwich wave.

sections.title: Colliding impulsive plane gravitational waves
sections.summary: Generalizes the Rosen form so all metric functions depend on both u and v, and quotes the Penrose-Khan vacuum solution built from p = u theta(u), q = v theta(v). Four regions are identified: flat region I before either wave, flat regions II and III each crossed by one wave, and curved interaction region IV. An observer at x = 0 meets both waves at t = 0 and reaches a curvature singularity at u^2 + v^2 = 1 in finite proper time. The lines u = 1 in II and v = 1 in III are fold singularities (caustics where null geodesics cross), not curvature singularities. The authors warn that the diagram makes escape through u = 1 look possible when it is not, note a step discontinuity in curvature on the post-collision wavefronts, and conclude that the waves focus each other into an unavoidable spacelike singularity.
key_moves: Generalized Rosen ansatz l du dv - f^2 dy^2 - g^2 dz^2 with l, f, g functions of u and v.
Penrose-Khan functions in terms of p, q, r, w, m; region of validity bounded by u = 1, v = 1 and u^2 + v^2 = 1.

Classify curvature by region: zero in I-III, delta on the incoming fronts, a finite (step) jump in addition to the delta on the two wavefront segments that bound region IV (u = 0 with 0 < v < 1, v = 0 with 0 < u < 1), divergent at u^2 + v^2 = 1.
Distinguish fold (caustic) singularities from scalar-invariant blow-up.
Argue that an observer near the caustic cannot escape and ends on the spacelike singularity.

sections.title: Colliding gravitational waves
sections.summary: Asks whether the singularity is an artefact of high symmetry, as had once been suspected for Schwarzschild. Szekeres recast colliding waves as a characteristic initial value problem with data on u = 0 and v = 0 and showed the interaction region is uniquely determined. Assuming two commuting translational Killing vectors everywhere, the metric takes a Rosen-type form with four functions M, U, V, W; in regions II and III these depend on only one null coordinate, and for constant parallel polarizations W = 0 and the problem reduces to an integral for V and quadratures for M. Sandwich-wave collisions also end in singularities. The section closes by noting many later exact solutions (with electromagnetic fields, fluids, null dust) and the unresolved question of whether colliding null dust streams interpenetrate or become a stiff fluid. The authors end by stressing that such collision problems mix initial-value and boundary-value features, so both the formulation and the physical reading of the resulting solutions need care.
key_moves: Pose the collision as data on two intersecting null hypersurfaces with a flat region I.
Well-posedness: given data determine region IV uniquely.
Szekeres metric with functions M, U, V, W; reduction to one-null-coordinate dependence in II and III.
Parallel constant polarizations allow W = 0 and reduce the problem to an integral plus quadratures.
Sandwich-wave collisions still singular, so the singularity is not an artefact of impulsiveness.
Flag interpretive ambiguity in matter-coupled collisions (null dust versus stiff fluid).

sections.title: Exercises and further reading
sections.summary: Seven exercises complete the omitted verifications: the gamma integrability condition, the complex pulse solution, the Rosen connection and field equation, the Rosen-to-Brinkmann map and its inverse, a rescaled Rosen convention, distribution identities, and the impulsive-wave curvature. Further reading points to Kramer et al. for exact solutions, Thorne (1965) for Einstein-Rosen waves, and Griffiths (1991) for colliding waves.

concepts.name: exact solution
aliases: solution of the full field equations
concepts.definition: A metric satisfying the complete non-linear Einstein equations with no perturbative truncation, as opposed to a solution of the linearized equations about flat space.
concepts.how_introduced: Opening contrast with Chapter 21: instead of small ripples, the chapter seeks full vacuum solutions that still describe radiation, using symmetry to make the search tractable.

concepts.name: Birkhoff's theorem
concepts.definition: Any spherically symmetric vacuum solution is, in the exterior region, necessarily static (locally Schwarzschild), so spherical symmetry cannot support vacuum gravitational radiation.
concepts.how_introduced: Invoked in one line to rule out the simplest symmetry assumption and motivate two-Killing-vector symmetry.

concepts.name: Killing vector
concepts.definition: A vector field X along which the metric is unchanged, L_X g_ab = 0, equivalently nabla_(a X_b) = 0; its flow is a continuous symmetry of space-time.
concepts.how_introduced: Used as the language of symmetry: spherical symmetry has three rotational spacelike Killing vectors, and the wave solutions assume two.

concepts.name: commuting Killing vectors
concepts.definition: Two independent spacelike Killing vectors V, W with vanishing Lie bracket, so coordinates can be chosen in which both are coordinate basis vectors and the metric is independent of the two corresponding coordinates.
concepts.how_introduced: Assumed as the next-simplest symmetry after spherical; the authors justify commutation from the surface-forming property of the orbits with a pointer to (10.15).
concepts.notes: Frobenius alone only puts [V,W] in the span of V and W; commutation additionally reflects the abelian structure of the symmetry groups used (rotation x translation, or two translations).

concepts.name: orbit topology of Killing vectors
concepts.definition: The global shape of the integral curves of a Killing vector: closed circles (S^1) for rotations, open lines (R) for translations; the combination distinguishes cylindrical from plane symmetry.
concepts.how_introduced: Used as the classification criterion right after [V,W]=0 is established.

concepts.name: cylindrical symmetry
concepts.definition: A space-time with two commuting spacelike Killing vectors, one generating rotations with closed 2pi-periodic orbits and one generating translations along an axis, so metric components depend only on t and a radial coordinate.
concepts.how_introduced: Adapted coordinates (t, rho, phi, z) with Killing vectors d/dphi and d/dz.

concepts.name: whole-cylinder symmetry
aliases: reflection symmetry in phi and z
concepts.definition: The additional discrete invariance of a cylindrically symmetric metric under z -> -z and phi -> -phi, which removes all cross terms between dphi or dz and the other coordinates.
concepts.how_introduced: Stated as an extra assumption right after the adapted coordinates are set up, with the name credited to authors such as Thorne (1965); the book translates it at once into the absence of dphi dx^a and dz dx^a cross terms.
concepts.notes: Reviewer gloss, not in the book: a diagonal metric of this kind carries a single fixed polarization, which is why the Einstein-Rosen family has one dynamical function psi.

concepts.name: adapted coordinates
concepts.definition: Coordinates in which the given Killing vectors are coordinate basis fields, so the metric components do not depend on the corresponding coordinates.
concepts.how_introduced: Constructed first for cylindrical symmetry and then for plane symmetry (d/dy, d/dz), with the star-equals notation marking coordinate-dependent statements.

concepts.name: conformal flatness of two-dimensional metrics
concepts.definition: Every two-dimensional metric can locally be written as a positive function times a flat metric; for Lorentzian signature, E(t,rho)(dt^2 - drho^2), obtained by taking null curves as coordinate lines.
concepts.how_introduced: Quoted from Section 6.13 to simplify the (t, rho) block of the cylindrical metric.
concepts.notes: The theorem in 6.13 is stated for Riemannian 2-manifolds; the Lorentzian version needed here is Exercise 6.31.

concepts.name: Einstein-Rosen metric
concepts.definition: The whole-cylinder-symmetric line element e^{2gamma-2psi}(dt^2 - drho^2) - rho^2 e^{-2psi} dphi^2 - e^{2psi} dz^2, with psi(t,rho) and gamma(t,rho) as the only unknowns.
concepts.how_introduced: Reached in three coordinate steps: radial coordinate from the orbit coefficients, psi from the z-coefficient, conformal gauge for the remaining 2-metric.
concepts.notes: The book calls (22.4) the general cylindrically symmetric metric, but it was derived under the whole-cylinder (reflection) assumption and a spacelike gradient of the area radius; general cylindrical waves with two polarizations need cross terms.

concepts.name: cylindrical wave equation
aliases: axisymmetric flat-space wave equation for psi
concepts.definition: psi_tt - (1/rho)(rho psi_rho)_rho = 0: the ordinary linear wave equation in flat 3-space for a field independent of phi and z; in Einstein-Rosen waves it is the full content of the dynamics.
concepts.how_introduced: Emerges from the vacuum equations for the Einstein-Rosen metric, highlighted as an unexpected linear core inside non-linear GR.

concepts.name: integrability condition for gamma
concepts.definition: The requirement that mixed partial derivatives of gamma agree, which holds for (22.6)-(22.7) precisely when psi satisfies the cylindrical wave equation, so gamma follows by line integration.
concepts.how_introduced: Noted as a consistency check after the field equations are stated; verification is Exercise 22.1.

concepts.name: Bessel-mode solutions
concepts.definition: Separable solutions psi = A J0(omega rho) cos(omega t) + B N0(omega rho) sin(omega t) of the cylindrical wave equation; regularity on the axis requires B = 0 since N0 diverges at rho = 0.
concepts.how_introduced: Obtained by separation of variables; used to illustrate that gamma can then be integrated and to recall Einstein and Rosen's worries about singular behaviour.

concepts.name: Weber-Wheeler pulse
concepts.definition: A regular cylindrical wave packet formed by superposing J0 modes with an exponential frequency weight, with closed form C[(a - it)^2 + rho^2]^{-1/2} + c.c.; it implodes onto the axis and re-expands, carries energy, and has a closed-form gamma.
concepts.how_introduced: Presented as the more interesting solution that refuted Einstein and Rosen's belief that such waves were unphysical.
concepts.notes: On the axis psi(t,0) = 2Ca/(a^2+t^2), a Lorentzian pulse of width a (our evaluation). The book misprints the weight as e^{a omega}; convergence needs e^{-a omega}.

concepts.name: coordinate singularity versus physical singularity
concepts.definition: A coordinate singularity is a breakdown of a particular chart or metric representation that disappears in better coordinates; a physical (intrinsic) singularity is signalled by divergence of curvature scalar invariants.
concepts.how_introduced: Appears twice: historically in Einstein and Rosen's doubts about their waves, and in the Penrose-Khan analysis separating fold singularities from the curvature singularity.

concepts.name: plane symmetry
concepts.definition: Two commuting spacelike Killing vectors whose orbits are both open lines, realized as translations d/dy and d/dz, so the metric depends only on t and x (or u and v).
concepts.how_introduced: Introduced as the second branch of the orbit-topology classification and made concrete with translations in y and z.

concepts.name: double null coordinates
concepts.definition: Coordinates u = t - x and v = t + x whose level sets are null hypersurfaces; the flat 2-metric dt^2 - dx^2 becomes du dv.
concepts.how_introduced: Introduced to rewrite the linearized h22 wave, then used for every plane and colliding wave in the chapter.

concepts.name: h22 wave
concepts.definition: The linearized plane wave of Chapter 21 with metric perturbation h22 = -h33 depending on t - x, which stretches y and squeezes z alternately.
concepts.how_introduced: Used as the seed for the exact Rosen ansatz.

concepts.name: Rosen form of a plane wave
concepts.definition: The plane-wave line element du dv - f^2(u) dy^2 - g^2(u) dz^2 in which freely falling particles sit at constant (y, z) and the transverse geometry is encoded in scale factors f and g.
concepts.how_introduced: Obtained by squaring the linearized h22 coefficients and taking the result as an exact ansatz; generalized in 22.5 to l du dv - f^2 dy^2 - g^2 dz^2 with u and v dependence.
concepts.notes: Rosen coordinates degenerate where f or g vanish even when curvature is finite (the fold singularities of 22.5).

concepts.name: linearly polarized exact plane gravitational wave
concepts.definition: A vacuum solution in Rosen form with f''/f + g''/g = 0, fixed by an arbitrary profile h(u); it represents a plane-fronted wave of constant polarization travelling in +x with no source.
concepts.how_introduced: The field equation collapses to one ODE; naming f''/f = h and solving g''/g = -h produces a family labelled by an arbitrary function.
prerequisites: Rosen form of a plane wave

concepts.name: wave profile function h(u)
concepts.definition: The freely specifiable function of retarded time u that sets the curvature (and hence tidal strength) of an exact plane wave: h = f''/f = -g''/g in Rosen form and the coefficient of (Z^2 - Y^2) dU^2 in Brinkmann form.
concepts.how_introduced: Named as a convenience in solving the field equation and identified as the wave amplitude through the Brinkmann form.
prerequisites: linearly polarized exact plane gravitational wave

concepts.name: Brinkmann form of a plane wave
concepts.definition: The plane-wave line element h(U)(Z^2 - Y^2) dU^2 + dU dV - dY^2 - dZ^2: flat space plus a single term quadratic in the transverse coordinates, with the profile appearing explicitly.
concepts.how_introduced: Reached from Rosen form via (22.16); the authors use it to exhibit the free function and the limited superposition principle.
prerequisites: Rosen form of a plane wave
coordinate transformation of a line element

concepts.name: non-linearity and failure of superposition
concepts.definition: Because the field equations are non-linear, the sum of two vacuum solutions is generally not a solution, so gravitational waves can scatter each other, unlike electromagnetic waves in vacuum.
concepts.how_introduced: Set against the linearity of Maxwell theory to motivate studying wave collisions.

concepts.name: exact superposition of co-propagating plane waves
concepts.definition: Plane waves moving in the same direction can be combined exactly by adding their Brinkmann profile functions, because the Brinkmann metric is linear in h; hence they do not scatter each other.
concepts.how_introduced: Read off from the structure of (22.17).
prerequisites: Brinkmann form of a plane wave

concepts.name: head-on frame for colliding waves
concepts.definition: For two plane waves meeting at an angle, a suitable boost produces observers who see them approaching along a common line from opposite directions, so it suffices to study head-on collisions.
concepts.how_introduced: Asserted with reference to the photon version, Exercise 4.10.

concepts.name: Heaviside step function
concepts.definition: theta(u) = 0 for u <= 0 and 1 for u > 0; its distributional derivative is the Dirac delta.
concepts.how_introduced: Introduced as a mathematical digression before constructing impulsive waves.

concepts.name: Dirac delta distribution
concepts.definition: A distribution defined by its action under an integral, picking out the value of a smooth test function at zero; informally zero away from the origin with unit integral.
concepts.how_introduced: Given a working definition, with a caution that it is not a genuine function, plus identities theta' = delta, u delta = 0, u theta' = 0.

concepts.name: impulsive plane gravitational wave
concepts.definition: A plane-wave vacuum space-time whose curvature is a delta function supported on a single null hypersurface u = 0, with flat space on both sides; in Rosen form f = 1 + u theta(u), g = 1 - u theta(u), and in Brinkmann form h = delta(U).
concepts.how_introduced: Built by choosing Rosen functions with a kink at u = 0 and checking the field equation with distribution identities; pictured spatially and in a space-time diagram.
prerequisites: Rosen form of a plane wave
Brinkmann form of a plane wave
concepts.notes: Physically the wave gives freely falling particles an instantaneous transverse kick: afterwards y-separations grow and z-separations shrink linearly in u, so z-neighbours meet at u = 1 (our reading of f and g).

concepts.name: sandwich wave
concepts.definition: A curved vacuum region confined between two parallel null hypersurfaces, with flat space before and after; an impulsive wave is its limit as the slab thickness goes to zero.
concepts.how_introduced: Defined with a three-region space-time diagram and used to describe what a geodesic observer experiences; later Szekeres' more realistic collisions use sandwich waves.
prerequisites: linearly polarized exact plane gravitational wave
Weyl tensor equals Riemann tensor in vacuum

concepts.name: Weyl tensor equals Riemann tensor in vacuum
concepts.definition: When the Ricci tensor vanishes, the Weyl (trace-free) part of curvature is the whole Riemann tensor, so vacuum curvature is purely tidal and free.
concepts.how_introduced: Parenthetical remark when listing the non-zero impulsive-wave curvature components.

concepts.name: transverse tidal acceleration in a plane wave
aliases: geodesic deviation in a plane wave
concepts.definition: Neighbouring freely falling particles in a plane wave accelerate relative to one another only in the directions perpendicular to propagation, with sign opposite in the two polarization axes.
concepts.how_introduced: Mentioned for an observer crossing a sandwich wave; builds on the tidal picture of Chapter 21.

concepts.name: colliding plane gravitational waves
concepts.definition: The non-linear interaction of two counter-propagating plane gravitational waves, modelled by metrics depending on both null coordinates, in which the waves scatter and focus each other.
concepts.how_introduced: Motivated by the failure of superposition and made tractable by the head-on frame and impulsive idealization.

concepts.name: Penrose-Khan solution
concepts.definition: The exact vacuum solution for two colliding linearly polarized impulsive plane waves: flat regions I-III, a curved interaction region IV ending in a spacelike curvature singularity at u^2 + v^2 = 1, and fold singularities at u = 1 and v = 1.
concepts.how_introduced: Quoted in closed form with a region-by-region space-time diagram.
concepts.notes: In region II (q = 0) the functions reduce to l = 1, f = 1 + u, g = 1 - u, recovering the single impulsive wave (22.24); we checked this symbolically.

concepts.name: interaction region
concepts.definition: The part of a colliding-wave space-time that lies to the future of both incoming wavefronts, where both waves are present and the metric depends on u and v.
concepts.how_introduced: Labelled region IV in both Fig. 22.4 and Fig. 22.5.

concepts.name: mutual focusing and caustics
aliases: focusing of null geodesics by a wave
concepts.definition: Each plane wave acts like a lens on null rays and test particles crossing it; rays converge and cross on caustic surfaces, and in a collision each wave focuses the other's wavefront.
concepts.how_introduced: Used to explain both the fold singularities at u = 1, v = 1 and, ultimately, the curvature singularity.

concepts.name: fold singularity
concepts.definition: A surface where the Rosen-type coordinates degenerate because the null geodesic generators used to build them cross; curvature invariants stay finite, so it is not an intrinsic singularity.
concepts.how_introduced: Identified at u = 1 in region II and v = 1 in region III of the Penrose-Khan solution, described as a seam in the v = 0 (or u = 0) hypersurface.

concepts.name: curvature singularity
concepts.definition: A place where curvature scalar invariants built from the Riemann tensor diverge, so no change of coordinates can remove it.
concepts.how_introduced: The fate of region IV in the Penrose-Khan solution, reached by the observer x = 0 in finite proper time.

concepts.name: spacelike versus timelike singularity
concepts.definition: A spacelike singularity lies to the future of every observer in the region approaching it and cannot be dodged; a timelike singularity is a place in space that observers can steer around.
concepts.how_introduced: Used to summarize the Penrose-Khan result, recalling black-hole singularities from earlier chapters.

concepts.name: step wave
concepts.definition: A wavefront carrying a finite jump in the curvature tensor (a discontinuity rather than a delta function), which appears on the fronts u = 0, 0 < v < 1 and v = 0, 0 < u < 1 after the collision, in addition to the delta part.
concepts.how_introduced: Noted briefly while listing curvature features of the Penrose-Khan space-time.

concepts.name: characteristic initial value problem
concepts.definition: Prescribing field data on a pair of intersecting null hypersurfaces (here u = 0 and v = 0 meeting in a spacelike 2-surface) and solving for the region to their common future; for colliding waves it is well posed.
concepts.how_introduced: Presented as the core of Szekeres' framework with Fig. 22.5; full treatment deferred to Section 23.5.

concepts.name: Szekeres colliding-wave metric
concepts.definition: The general metric for plane-symmetric colliding waves with two translational Killing vectors: e^{-M} du dv - e^{-U}(e^V cosh W dy^2 - 2 sinh W dy dz + e^{-V} cosh W dz^2), with M, U, V, W functions of u and v.
concepts.how_introduced: Quoted as the outcome of Szekeres' analysis; one-variable dependence in regions II and III, and W = 0 for parallel polarizations.
prerequisites: Rosen form of a plane wave

concepts.name: collinear (parallel) polarization
concepts.definition: The case where both colliding waves have fixed polarization axes aligned with each other, allowing the metric to be diagonal (W = 0) everywhere.
concepts.how_introduced: Condition under which Szekeres' problem reduces to an integral for V and quadratures for M.

concepts.name: null dust
concepts.definition: Matter with energy-momentum tensor of dust form rho_0 u^a u^b but with a null vector in place of a timelike 4-velocity, modelling incoherent radiation moving at light speed.
concepts.how_introduced: Mentioned among later colliding-wave models and in the controversy about colliding waves followed by null dust.

concepts.name: stiff fluid
aliases: stiff equation of state p = rho
concepts.definition: A perfect fluid whose pressure equals its energy density, so the sound speed equals the speed of light.
concepts.how_introduced: Posed as one possible outcome of colliding null dust streams, illustrating interpretive ambiguity.

key_equations.name: Commuting Killing vectors
key_equations.meaning: The two spacelike symmetry generators commute, so both can be made coordinate vector fields at once.
key_equations.symbols: V, W spacelike Killing vectors; [ , ] Lie bracket

key_equations.name: Whole-cylinder-symmetric metric
key_equations.meaning: Reflection symmetry in phi and z removes cross terms, leaving a (t, rho) block and two positive orbit coefficients.
key_equations.symbols: C, D positive functions; x^A = (t, rho)

key_equations.name: Area radius and potential psi
key_equations.meaning: Choose the radial coordinate so that the Killing-orbit part of the metric has determinant rho^2, and encode the remaining freedom in psi.
key_equations.symbols: rho-tilde new radial coordinate; psi scalar potential

key_equations.latex: ds^2=\tilde g_{AB}\,d\tilde x^A d\tilde x^B-\tilde\rho^2 e^{-2\psi}d\phi^2-e^{2\psi}dz^2
key_equations.meaning: Intermediate cylindrical metric after the change to area radius.
key_equations.symbols: g-tilde_AB depends on (t-tilde, rho-tilde)

key_equations.latex: d\sigma^2=\tilde g_{00}\,d\tilde t^2+2\tilde g_{01}\,d\tilde t\,d\tilde\rho+\tilde g_{11}\,d\tilde\rho^2
key_equations.meaning: The 2-metric on the (t, rho) surfaces orthogonal to the Killing orbits.
key_equations.symbols: sigma 2-dimensional line element

key_equations.name: Conformal gauge
key_equations.meaning: Any Lorentzian 2-metric is conformally flat; the conformal factor is written so the final metric looks symmetric in psi.
key_equations.symbols: E conformal factor; gamma second metric function

key_equations.name: Einstein-Rosen metric
key_equations.meaning: General whole-cylinder-symmetric metric in terms of two functions of t and rho.
key_equations.symbols: psi(t,rho), gamma(t,rho); phi 2pi-periodic

key_equations.name: Cylindrical wave equation
key_equations.meaning: The dynamical vacuum equation: psi obeys the flat-space wave equation with cylindrical symmetry.
key_equations.symbols: psi Einstein-Rosen potential

key_equations.meaning: Radial gradient of gamma is fixed by an energy-density-like quadratic in psi derivatives, so gamma grows outward wherever the wave has energy.
key_equations.symbols: gamma second metric function

key_equations.meaning: Time derivative of gamma is a flux-like product; together with (22.6) gamma follows by quadrature.

key_equations.name: Integrability condition
key_equations.meaning: Mixed derivatives of gamma must agree; this holds automatically once psi solves (22.5).

key_equations.name: Bessel modes
key_equations.meaning: Separable monochromatic cylindrical waves; axis regularity forces B = 0.
key_equations.symbols: J0, N0 Bessel functions of first and second kind; omega angular frequency

key_equations.name: Weber-Wheeler pulse
key_equations.meaning: A regular pulse built from J0 modes; the two terms are complex conjugates so psi is real.
key_equations.symbols: C amplitude constant (length); a > 0 pulse width

key_equations.name: gamma for the Weber-Wheeler pulse (corrected)
key_equations.meaning: Closed-form second metric function; it vanishes on the axis (regularity) and tends to C^2/a^2 at large rho.
key_equations.symbols: Printed with (a^2+rho^2) not squared; we verified numerically that only the squared version satisfies (22.6)-(22.7).

key_equations.name: Double null coordinates
key_equations.meaning: Null coordinates adapted to waves moving in +x (constant u) and -x (constant v).

key_equations.name: Rosen form
key_equations.meaning: Exact plane-wave ansatz with transverse scale factors depending on retarded time only.
key_equations.symbols: f, g functions of u

key_equations.meaning: Links the Rosen functions to the linearized h22 wave for small epsilon.
key_equations.symbols: epsilon small parameter; h22 linearized perturbation

key_equations.name: Rosen connection
key_equations.meaning: Only non-zero Christoffel symbols (up to symmetry) of the Rosen metric.
key_equations.symbols: x^a = (u, v, y, z); prime d/du

key_equations.name: Rosen curvature
key_equations.meaning: The two independent Riemann components; the transverse scale factors' accelerations are the tidal field.
key_equations.symbols: Index 0 = u, 2 = y, 3 = z

key_equations.name: Plane-wave vacuum equation
key_equations.meaning: The single vacuum field equation for the Rosen ansatz (the uu Ricci component).
Definition of the profile function h(u).
key_equations.symbols: h(u) arbitrary profile

key_equations.meaning: Second scale factor chosen to cancel the first in the Ricci tensor.

key_equations.name: Rosen-to-Brinkmann map
key_equations.meaning: Coordinate change that absorbs the transverse scale factors into physical transverse distances.

key_equations.name: Brinkmann form
key_equations.meaning: Plane wave as flat space plus a term quadratic in transverse position; linear in h, so co-moving waves superpose.
key_equations.symbols: U, V, Y, Z Brinkmann coordinates

key_equations.name: Brinkmann geodesic deviation (our derivation, not printed)
key_equations.meaning: Transverse equations of motion of free particles in (22.17); with h = delta they give a velocity kick proportional to position.
key_equations.symbols: U affine parameter along geodesics

key_equations.name: Heaviside step
key_equations.meaning: Step function used to switch on the wave at u = 0.
Delta vanishes away from the origin.

key_equations.name: Sifting property
key_equations.meaning: Operational definition of the delta distribution.
key_equations.symbols: f smooth test function

key_equations.meaning: Derivative of the step is the delta.
Delta times a function vanishing at 0 is zero.
Equivalent form of (22.22).

key_equations.name: Derivative identity (Exercise 22.6)
key_equations.meaning: Consequence of integrating by parts against a test function.

key_equations.name: Impulsive-wave Rosen functions
key_equations.meaning: Transverse scale factors that are 1 before the wave and change linearly afterwards.
Distributional derivatives confirm the vacuum equation (22.13).

key_equations.name: Impulsive-wave curvature
key_equations.meaning: Curvature is concentrated on the null plane u = 0; Ricci is zero.
Brinkmann profile of the impulsive wave.
Off the wavefront the impulsive wave is Minkowski space in null coordinates.

key_equations.name: Generalized Rosen form
key_equations.meaning: Ansatz allowing waves moving in both directions.
key_equations.symbols: ell conformal factor of the (u,v) block

key_equations.name: Penrose-Khan solution
key_equations.meaning: Exact vacuum space-time of two colliding impulsive plane waves.

key_equations.name: Penrose-Khan auxiliary functions
key_equations.meaning: p and q switch on after each wave; m vanishes on the singularity.

key_equations.name: Penrose-Khan regions
key_equations.meaning: Domain of validity divided into three flat regions and one curved interaction region.

key_equations.name: Szekeres colliding-wave metric
key_equations.meaning: General plane-symmetric collision metric; W = 0 for parallel constant polarizations.
key_equations.symbols: M, U, V, W functions of (u,v) (not the Brinkmann coordinates)

key_equations.name: Complex seed solution (Exercise 22.2)
key_equations.meaning: Complex solution of (22.5) whose real part gives the Weber-Wheeler pulse.

key_equations.name: Alternative Rosen normalization (Exercise 22.5)
key_equations.latex: ds^2=2\,d\bar u\,d\bar v-\bar f^2(\bar u)\,d\bar y^2-\bar g^2(\bar u)\,d\bar z^2
key_equations.meaning: Convention with a factor 2 on the null term, related to (22.10) by rescaling; the printed exercise has g-bar depending on v-bar, likely a slip.

figures.caption_paraphrase: No caption; page-design element rather than a physics figure.
figures.visual_description: A tall, narrow strip ruled into two columns of small square cells (roughly twenty rows), with a few slightly heavier horizontal rules. The page renders show the same grid in the outer margin of pages 470-474 wherever no margin figure sits; only this copy was exported as an image.
figures.what_it_teaches: Nothing physical; it is the book's decorative margin grid.

figures.label: Fig. 22.1
figures.caption_paraphrase: Spatial view of an impulsive plane gravitational wave.
figures.visual_description: Perspective 3D axes: z up, x to the right, y receding toward the lower left. A parallelogram representing a plane perpendicular to x cuts through the x-axis. An arrow from the plane points in +x labelled 'Speed = 1'. The word 'Flat' is printed on each side of the plane.
figures.what_it_teaches: An impulsive wave is a single plane front moving at light speed with flat space-time on both sides.

redesign.idea: A 3D scene with a translucent plane sweeping along x through a cubic lattice of free test particles, which are at rest until the plane touches them and then drift: spreading in y, converging in z, meeting at the focal distance.
redesign.interaction: Slider for wave strength (inverse focal length), toggle + or x polarization, scrub time; clicking a particle pair plots its separation versus time with the kink at the front.

figures.label: Fig. 22.2
figures.caption_paraphrase: Space-time diagram (two transverse dimensions dropped) of an impulsive plane wave.
figures.visual_description: Axes t (vertical) and x (horizontal). A straight 45-degree line through the origin is labelled 'u = 0', with a pointer label 'R_abcd ~ delta'. The regions above-left and below-right of the line are each labelled 'Flat'.
figures.what_it_teaches: The curvature of an impulsive wave lives on one null hypersurface; every event off it is in flat space.

redesign.idea: Linked panels: a (t, x) diagram with the null wavefront, plus a transverse panel showing a ring of particles. Dragging a world line across u = 0 updates the ring shape and a plot of Y(U), Z(U) with slope jumps.
redesign.interaction: Drag the observer event; switch between Rosen coordinates (particles fixed, grid deforms) and Brinkmann coordinates (grid fixed, particles move).

figures.label: Fig. 22.3
figures.caption_paraphrase: Space-time diagram of a sandwich wave.
figures.visual_description: Axes t (vertical) and x (horizontal). A hatched band between two parallel lines rising to the right forms region II, annotated 'R_abcd != 0, R_ab = 0', with a pointer 'Non-flat' at its lower-left end. Region III sits above the band near the t-axis and region I below it to the right; the flat side labels read 'Flat, R_abcd = R_ab = 0'.
figures.what_it_teaches: A sandwich wave is a curved but Ricci-flat slab between flat regions; an observer crosses I, then II, then III and feels a tidal effect only while inside II.
concepts: Weyl tensor equals Riemann tensor in vacuum

redesign.idea: Sandwich-to-impulse limit explorer: choose a profile h(u) (Gaussian, square, sine burst) whose thickness shrinks at fixed integrated strength while the band on the diagram thins and the observer's separation curves become straight segments joined by a kink.
redesign.interaction: Thickness slider, profile picker, observer world-line drag; live curves of transverse separations and of h(u).

figures.label: Fig. 22.4
figures.caption_paraphrase: Penrose-Khan space-time diagram for two colliding impulsive plane waves.
figures.visual_description: A (t, x) diagram with small axes at the origin. Two null lines come in from the lower left and lower right, labelled 'Impulsive wave u = 0' and 'Impulsive wave v = 0', with 'R_abcd ~ delta' at their lower ends. Region I at the bottom is 'Flat (R_abcd = 0)'. They cross at the origin and continue upward to meet a wavy arc labelled 'Singularity u^2 + v^2 = 1'. Between them is region IV 'Curved'. Region II (left) and III (right) are 'Flat', each bounded on its outer side by a wavy line parallel to the incoming wave, labelled 'Caustic 2-surface' with 'u = 1' and 'v = 1'.
figures.what_it_teaches: The collision creates a curved region that ends on a spacelike singularity, while each single-wave region is flat but terminated by a caustic fold; curvature type is region-dependent.

redesign.idea: Interactive (u, v) map of the Penrose-Khan solution: hovering shows the region, metric functions l, f, g and a curvature indicator; the user launches timelike observers from region I and watches them hit the singularity, with a proper-time counter.
redesign.interaction: Click to launch observers with chosen velocity; toggle rotated (t, x) or (u, v) axes; show how f and g shrink toward the caustic and the singularity.

figures.label: Fig. 22.5
figures.caption_paraphrase: Characteristic initial value problem for colliding waves.
figures.visual_description: Two crossing null lines forming an X, labelled 'u = 0' (lower left) and 'v = 0' (lower right). Region I is at the bottom, II left, III right, IV top. Arrows along the upper branches are labelled u and v, showing the direction in which each coordinate increases. A label 'Initial data prescribed' points to both upper branches bounding region IV.
figures.what_it_teaches: Specifying data on the two null boundaries of the interaction region determines the solution inside it uniquely.

redesign.idea: Characteristic-data sandbox: the learner sketches wave profiles along the two null boundaries, and the app shades region IV as the domain determined by that data and, for collinear polarization, evolves the metric function numerically on a (u, v) grid, flagging where the transverse area collapses.
redesign.interaction: Draw or pick profiles for each incoming wave; scrub a marching front across the grid; toggle impulsive versus sandwich data.

worked_examples.problem: Put the general whole-cylinder-symmetric metric into a canonical form with as few free functions as possible.
worked_examples.method: Use discrete reflections to kill cross terms; choose the square root of the product of the orbit coefficients as radius and half the log of the z coefficient as psi; apply conformal flatness to the (t, rho) block and write the factor as exp(2 gamma - 2 psi).
worked_examples.key_insight: Symmetry plus two coordinate freedoms leave only two unknown functions, and the chosen radius makes the orbit area explicit.

worked_examples.problem: Solve the Einstein-Rosen vacuum equations by separation of variables.
worked_examples.method: Separate psi into a radial times a harmonic time factor; the radial equation is Bessel's of order zero; reject N0 for axis regularity; integrate (22.6)-(22.7) for gamma.
worked_examples.key_insight: The non-linear system has a linear core, so standard mathematical physics applies to psi.

worked_examples.problem: Build a localized cylindrical pulse and its gamma (Weber and Wheeler).
worked_examples.method: Superpose J0 cos modes with an exponential weight; evaluate the integral using the Laplace-type transform of J0 to get a conjugate pair; integrate the gamma equations in closed form.
worked_examples.key_insight: A regular, finite-energy exact gravitational wave exists, answering the historical doubt.
worked_examples.result: psi = C[(a-it)^2+rho^2]^{-1/2} + c.c.; gamma as displayed (with the misprints corrected).

worked_examples.problem: Decide whether the linearized h22 metric can be made an exact vacuum solution.
worked_examples.method: Write it in double null coordinates with squared transverse coefficients, compute the four Christoffel symbols and two Riemann components, and contract to Ricci.
worked_examples.key_insight: Only one field equation survives, so an arbitrary function generates a full family of exact solutions.
worked_examples.result: f''/f + g''/g = 0; define h = f''/f and solve g''/g = -h.
concepts: Rosen form of a plane wave
linearly polarized exact plane gravitational wave

worked_examples.problem: Rewrite the Rosen plane wave so the profile appears explicitly in the metric.
worked_examples.method: Apply U = u, V = v + y^2 ff' + z^2 gg', Y = fy, Z = gz; expand, cancel the cross terms, and use f'' = hf, g'' = -hg.
worked_examples.key_insight: The metric becomes flat space plus h(U)(Z^2 - Y^2) dU^2, linear in h, which exposes limited superposition.
worked_examples.result: Brinkmann form (22.17). The printed sign h(U)(Z^2 - Y^2) is correct: expanding gives dU dV - dY^2 = du dv - f^2 dy^2 + y^2 f f'' du^2, and f f'' y^2 = h Y^2 (re-derived by hand in review, and consistent with the Brinkmann geodesic equation d^2Y/dU^2 = hY matching Y = f y with fixed y).
concepts: Brinkmann form of a plane wave
exact superposition of co-propagating plane waves

worked_examples.problem: Construct a plane wave whose curvature is a delta function on a null plane.
worked_examples.method: Choose f = 1 + u theta, g = 1 - u theta; differentiate using theta' = delta and u delta = 0; check (22.13); read off Riemann; translate to Brinkmann with h = delta.
worked_examples.key_insight: Distribution identities make the computation almost trivial and show the space-time is flat except on the front.
worked_examples.result: R_0202 = -R_0303 = delta(u), Ricci = 0, flat metric (22.28) off u = 0.

worked_examples.problem: Interpret the Penrose-Khan solution region by region.
worked_examples.method: Split the (u, v) plane by the signs of u and v; evaluate where the metric is flat, where curvature has delta or step parts, where Rosen coordinates fold (u = 1, v = 1), and where curvature invariants diverge (m = 0); follow the x = 0 observer.
worked_examples.key_insight: Each wave focuses the other; the focusing of the interaction region ends in an unavoidable spacelike singularity reached in finite proper time.
worked_examples.result: Regions I-III flat, IV curved; caustics at u = 1, v = 1; singularity at u^2 + v^2 = 1.

worked_examples.problem: Set up the general colliding plane-wave problem (Szekeres).
worked_examples.method: Pose data on u = 0 and v = 0 with flat region I; assume two translational Killing vectors everywhere; adopt the four-function metric; note one-variable dependence in II and III and W = 0 for collinear polarization.
worked_examples.key_insight: The collision becomes a well-posed characteristic problem, and the singularity persists for sandwich waves.
worked_examples.result: Reduction to an integral for V and quadratures for M in the collinear case.

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: Electromagnetic waves in vacuum pass through each other untouched, whereas gravitational waves need not.
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: Maxwell theory is used as the linear foil that makes the question of gravitational wave scattering meaningful.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: Even in GR, co-propagating plane waves superpose exactly, so the contrast only bites for waves moving in different directions.
analogies_and_intuitions.app_idea: Split screen: two EM pulses crossing unchanged versus two gravitational pulses that emerge distorted and focused.

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: An impulsive wave as the zero-thickness limit of a slab of curvature.
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: The sandwich wave is defined first as the physically sensible object; the delta-function wave is then read as its thin limit, justifying the idealization.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: The limit keeps the integrated strength fixed; quantities quadratic in curvature (energy density) are ill-defined for a delta profile.
analogies_and_intuitions.app_idea: Thickness slider that squeezes a smooth profile into a spike while the particle trajectories converge to a kinked limit.

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: A caustic as a seam in the wavefront hypersurface.
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: Explains why the u = 1 line on the diagram is not a door to escape through: it is a lower-dimensional crease in v = 0 that observers essentially never hit.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: The diagram suppresses two dimensions, so the 'seam' is hard to picture without a 3D view.
analogies_and_intuitions.app_idea: 3D view of the null hypersurface v = 0 with its generators converging and crossing along a highlighted crease.

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: A plane gravitational wave acts like an astigmatic lens (our framing, not in the book).
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: Suggested for tutoring: f = 1 + u and g = 1 - u after an impulsive wave mean rays spread in y and converge in z, meeting at a focal distance of one unit, exactly like a cylindrical lens.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: A lens acts on light in space; here the focusing acts on all geodesics and the 'focal length' is a null affine distance.
analogies_and_intuitions.app_idea: Ray-optics style panel: parallel null rays cross an impulsive wave and focus to a line; slider sets focal length.

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: The Einstein-Rosen potential psi behaves like a scalar ripple on a pond spreading from a long rod.
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: The book stresses that (22.5) is just the ordinary flat cylindrical wave equation, so all intuition about axisymmetric ripples transfers to psi.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: The geometry feels the wave through gamma, which accumulates non-linearly; psi's linearity does not make the space-time linear.
analogies_and_intuitions.app_idea: Animate a Weber-Wheeler pulse imploding and re-expanding, with a second trace of gamma(t, rho) growing behind it.

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: Suspecting that singularities come only from excessive symmetry, as once feared for Schwarzschild.
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: The authors recall the black-hole debate to motivate asking whether the collision singularity survives more general data, which Szekeres showed it does.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: Robustness under relaxing impulsiveness does not settle robustness under breaking plane symmetry, which the chapter does not address.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: A spherically pulsating or collapsing star should emit gravitational waves into the surrounding vacuum.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: Birkhoff's theorem makes any spherically symmetric vacuum exterior static, so no spherical gravitational radiation exists; waves need less symmetry.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Spherical sound or light pulses are familiar, and Newtonian intuition does not connect symmetry to time dependence.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: Gravitational waves superpose linearly, just like electromagnetic waves.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: The field equations are non-linear; only special cases such as co-propagating plane waves add exactly. Counter-propagating waves interact.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Chapter 21's linearized treatment and detector-physics experience are built on superposition.
concepts: exact superposition of co-propagating plane waves

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: Any two gravitational waves must scatter each other because GR is non-linear.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: Plane waves travelling in the same direction do not scatter: their Brinkmann profiles simply add.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Once non-linearity is emphasized, learners overgeneralize it to all configurations.
concepts: exact superposition of co-propagating plane waves

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: Oblique collisions of plane waves need a separate, harder analysis.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: A boost can always make the collision look head-on, so the head-on case is general.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: In a single frame the angle looks like physical information.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: If the Ricci and Einstein tensors vanish, space-time must be flat.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: Vacuum only kills Ricci; the Weyl part of Riemann can be non-zero, as the delta-function components of the impulsive wave show.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: The vacuum field equations are often summarized as 'curvature is zero where there is no matter'.
concepts: Weyl tensor equals Riemann tensor in vacuum

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: An impulsive gravitational wave curves the whole of space-time.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: Curvature is confined to the null plane u = 0; on either side the metric is exactly Minkowski, although crossing the front changes the relative velocities of free particles, so the two flat regions are not joined trivially.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Waves are usually pictured as extended oscillations filling space.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: The Dirac delta is an ordinary function that is infinite at zero.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: It is a distribution defined by its action under an integral; identities like u delta = 0 are statements about integrals against test functions.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Physics shorthand treats delta as a spike-shaped function.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: Einstein-Rosen waves are unphysical because their metric has singularities.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: The singularities Einstein and Rosen worried about were coordinate artefacts; Weber and Wheeler showed regular, energy-carrying pulses.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Singular metric components look like singular physics without an invariant check.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: The caustics at u = 1 and v = 1 in the Penrose-Khan solution are curvature singularities.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: They are fold singularities where null geodesics cross and the Rosen-type coordinates degenerate; curvature invariants remain finite there.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Metric functions vanish there and the diagram draws them with the same wavy line as the true singularity.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: An observer in region II can escape the collision by crossing the caustic at u = 1.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: The caustic is a thin seam that is practically never hit, and anyone approaching it is caught by the second wave and carried into the interaction region, ending on the spacelike singularity.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: In the suppressed-dimension diagram u = 1 looks like an open boundary leading away from the collision.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: The singularity from colliding waves is an artefact of impulsive (delta-function) waves or of excessive symmetry.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: Szekeres' sandwich-wave collisions also become singular; the effect comes from mutual focusing, not from the delta profile.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Idealized sources often produce idealized pathologies, and similar suspicions once surrounded Schwarzschild.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: After the collision, the space-time loses all its planar symmetry.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: The translational Killing vectors d/dy and d/dz persist throughout region IV (the Szekeres setup assumes it); what disappears is the pure plane-wave character of each wave. The book's phrase about losing planar symmetry should be read in that sense.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: The text states that the waves no longer have planar symmetry after impact.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: Coordinate singularities of Rosen coordinates indicate something physical happens where f or g vanish.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: Rosen coordinates tie the grid to freely falling particles, which a wave focuses; where they cross the chart fails. Brinkmann coordinates cover the same region smoothly.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: The metric determinant vanishes, which is usually alarming.
concepts: Rosen form of a plane wave
Brinkmann form of a plane wave

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: The exact plane wave is only valid for small amplitude because it came from linearized theory.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: Linearized theory only suggested the ansatz; the Rosen metric solves the full equations for any profile h(u).
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Equation (22.11) still contains the small parameter epsilon.
concepts: Rosen form of a plane wave
linearly polarized exact plane gravitational wave

thought_experiments.name: Riding through the collision at x = 0
thought_experiments.setup: An observer at rest at x = 0 in the flat region before two counter-propagating impulsive plane waves arrive; both waves reach the observer at t = 0.
thought_experiments.lesson: After the simultaneous hit the observer is inside a curved interaction region and meets a curvature singularity after a finite proper time; nothing can be done to avoid it.
thought_experiments.app_idea: Cockpit view with a proper-time clock and a transverse ring of particles that first shears then collapses as the singularity approaches (about 0.54 focal units of proper time, our estimate).

thought_experiments.name: Crossing a sandwich wave
thought_experiments.setup: A freely falling observer with nearby test particles passes from flat region I through curved slab II into flat region III.
thought_experiments.lesson: Tidal accelerations act only during the finite crossing and only transversely; before and after, relative motion is uniform.
concepts: transverse tidal acceleration in a plane wave
thought_experiments.app_idea: Timeline slider showing the ring of particles deforming only while the band passes the observer.

thought_experiments.name: Trying to escape through the caustic
thought_experiments.setup: An observer in region II heads toward the line u = 1 hoping to avoid the collision.
thought_experiments.lesson: The caustic is a measure-zero seam; approaching it means meeting the other wave and being carried into region IV's spacelike singularity.
thought_experiments.app_idea: Steerable world line on the Penrose-Khan map; every allowed path from region II ends on the singularity arc.

thought_experiments.name: Boosting an oblique collision head-on
thought_experiments.setup: Two plane waves cross at an angle in some frame; find observers moving so that the waves approach along a line.
thought_experiments.lesson: Head-on collision is a frame choice, so studying it loses no generality.
thought_experiments.app_idea: Aberration widget: rotate two wave vectors and slide a boost velocity until they are antiparallel.

thought_experiments.name: Colliding waves each trailed by null dust
thought_experiments.setup: Two planar impulsive waves, each followed by a stream of null dust, meet head-on.
thought_experiments.lesson: Exact solutions admit different interpretations (interpenetrating dust or a stiff fluid with p = rho), so formulation and interpretation must be handled with care.

applications_and_observations.topic: Plane waves as far-zone models of real radiation
applications_and_observations.details: The authors hope infinite plane waves capture properties of radiation from bounded sources far away. Our estimate of why this is reasonable at detectors: wavefront curvature radius equals the source distance, vastly larger than the wavelength.
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: Our estimate for a GW150914-like event: distance about 400 Mpc (about 1e22 km) versus wavelength about 1e3 to 1e4 km, so the front is flat to about one part in 1e18 across a wavelength.

applications_and_observations.topic: Proper time from collision to singularity for the x = 0 observer
applications_and_observations.details: Our calculation, not in the book: along u = v = t the Penrose-Khan conformal factor is (1 - 2t^2)^{3/2}/(1 - t^2), so proper time is the integral of its square root from t = 0 to 1/sqrt(2).
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: Coordinate time to singularity 1/sqrt(2), about 0.707; proper time about 0.543 (re-computed numerically in review: 0.5432), in units where each wave's focal length is 1.

applications_and_observations.topic: Focal length of an impulsive plane wave
applications_and_observations.details: Our reading of (22.24): after the wave, g = 1 - u, so particles initially separated in z at rest converge and meet at u = 1 while y-separations double by then. Restoring a strength parameter, f = 1 + u/L gives focal length L.
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: Focusing at u = 1 in the book's normalization; the fold singularity of Fig. 22.4 sits exactly there.

applications_and_observations.topic: Axis profile and asymptotic gamma of the Weber-Wheeler pulse
applications_and_observations.details: Our evaluation from (22.9) and the corrected gamma: on the axis the pulse is Lorentzian in time; far from the axis gamma tends to a constant, which shows up as a conical deficit of the outer geometry tied to the pulse energy per unit length (Thorne's C-energy).
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: psi(t, 0) = 2Ca/(a^2 + t^2); gamma(rho -> infinity) = C^2/a^2; gamma = 0 on the axis.

difficulty.notes: Short but dense. teaching_gems.gem: A symmetry ladder: start from spherical symmetry, see Birkhoff kill radiation, drop to two commuting Killing vectors, and let circle-versus-line orbit topology choose cylindrical or plane waves.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Learners see why these particular exact solutions exist instead of meeting them as a zoo.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Symmetry picker: toggle rotational and translational Killing fields on a 3D slice; the app reports what is forced (static, cylindrical, plane) and opens the matching wave demo.

teaching_gems.gem: The Einstein-Rosen system hides a flat, linear wave equation inside non-linear GR; the non-linearity is pushed into gamma, which is found afterwards by integration.
teaching_gems.why_effective: It demystifies exact solutions and lets learners reuse ordinary wave intuition.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Cylindrical ripple simulator: evolve psi from user-drawn initial data, then integrate gamma live and show the conical deficit building up at large radius.

teaching_gems.gem: Promote a linearized solution to an exact ansatz: square the coefficients of the h22 metric and find that the full equations reduce to one ODE with an arbitrary function.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Links Chapter 21 to exact theory and shows a reusable research tactic.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Toggle between linear h22 and exact Rosen f, g for a chosen profile; at large amplitude the linear version visibly fails (negative squared lengths) while the exact one stays consistent.

teaching_gems.gem: One wave, two coordinate systems: Rosen coordinates ride with free particles (grid deforms), Brinkmann coordinates are a fixed grid with particles moving; each makes different facts obvious.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Teaches coordinate freedom through a single concrete example with visible payoffs (caustics versus superposition).
teaching_gems.app_idea: Side-by-side transverse grids for the same plane wave, one comoving and one Brinkmann, with a slider through u and highlighted particle pairs.

teaching_gems.gem: An impulsive wave is two flat space-times glued along a null plane with a delta of curvature: free particles get a position-proportional velocity kick, spreading one way and focusing the other.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Curvature becomes a single, local, visualizable event rather than an abstract field.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Kick demo: a grid of dust particles passes through the front; arrows show the kick velocities; a timer shows z-neighbours meeting at the focal distance.

teaching_gems.gem: Consistency check (ours): set q = 0 in the Penrose-Khan functions and region II collapses to l = 1, f = 1 + u, g = 1 - u, the single impulsive wave; the fold at u = 1 is simply where that wave's focusing brings z-neighbours together.

teaching_gems.app_idea: Formula dissector: hover regions of the Penrose-Khan map to see the metric functions simplify symbolically region by region.

teaching_gems.gem: Read a collision off a labelled null diagram: flat, delta, step and divergent curvature each assigned to a region or boundary.

teaching_gems.app_idea: Penrose-Khan explorer with a curvature-type overlay and draggable observers carrying proper-time clocks.

teaching_gems.gem: Colliding waves as a characteristic initial value problem: specify data on two intersecting null surfaces and the interaction region is determined.
